title: Prescribed Weil filtrations on a finite clopen decomposition
statement:
Fix a prime power $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ as in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. On a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $S_0$ use the constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] on $S=S_0\times_{k_0}k$, with the common-stage constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart]. Restrictions are the inverse images of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], open extension by zero is the compact-support direct image of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and closed direct image is the direct image of [def-weil-derived-direct-image], all with their induced Weil structures. 
Let $N\in\mathbf N$ and let $S_0=\coprod_{b=1}^{N}V_{b,0}$ be a finite disjoint union of open and closed $k_0$-subschemes, with inclusions $h_{b,0}:V_{b,0}\hookrightarrow S_0$. Let $H$ be a constructible Weil sheaf on $S_0$. For each $b$ fix an integer $n_b\geq0$ and a particular filtration by constructible Weil subobjects
$$0=G_{b,0}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq G_{b,n_b}=h_b^*H,$$
whose quotients $Q_{b,s}=G_{b,s}/G_{b,s-1}$ are punctually $\iota$-pure of assigned real weights $v_{b,s}$, for $1\leq s\leq n_b$. Here $h_b$ is the geometric base change of $h_{b,0}$. There exists a finite filtration of $H$ by constructible Weil subobjects of length $\sum_{b=1}^{N}n_b$, whose successive quotients, in the order first $b$ then $s$, are Weil-isomorphic to $h_{b!}Q_{b,s}$ and are punctually pure of weights $v_{b,s}$. Consequently every common real upper bound of the $v_{b,s}$ is retained, with no requirement that the weights coincide or be ordered. The assertion allows zero sheaves, empty pieces and repeated filtration terms. If $N=0$, then $S_0=\varnothing$, $H=0$, and the resulting filtration is empty.

source.place: Penultimate paragraph, sentence “On a finite disjoint union, extend the filtrations of its components by zero and concatenate them”; old gluing proof step 5.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal A_b$ for the constructible Weil hearts on $S_0$ and $V_{b,0}$. The geometry and abelian assertions of [lem-zl-weil-heart-localization-exact] apply to these clopen subschemes. [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition] gives an equivalence induced by ordinary restriction to the $V_b$. On integral constructible objects this restriction is naturally isomorphic to the actual pullback $Lh_b^*$ by the canonical $\kappa$ of [lem-pur-open-completed-restriction-identification]. Hence at each finite coefficient field $r=(h_b^*)_b$ is naturally isomorphic to that equivalence, so it is one. At $\Qlb$, Hom sets are colimits over common finite stages; $r$ gives stagewise bijections compatible with the stage transitions, since the comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] are natural, so $r$ is fully faithful. A tuple is defined at one common finite stage, where it has a preimage whose image these comparisons identify after scalar extension; so $r$ is essentially surjective. By [lem-zl-immersion-weil-local-behavior](1), each $h_b^*$ is $t$-exact with $\mathcal H^a h_b^*\cong h_b^*\mathcal H^a$; as $r$ detects zero objects, $K$ lies in the heart iff every $h_b^*K$ does, so $r$ restricts to an equivalence of standard hearts. Each piece is defined over $k_0$, so $g_Sh_b=h_bg_{V_b}$. The natural comparison $\alpha_b:G_{V_b}h_b^*\simeq h_b^*G_S$ is the one in [lem-zl-open-weil-unit-and-empty-fibre]. Apply [lem-fd-fixed-pair-equivalence-transport] to $r$ and $b=(\alpha_b^{-1})_b$: its transported structure is exactly $(h_b^*\theta\circ\alpha_b)_b$. Fixed pairs in the product are tuples of fixed pairs. We obtain an equivalence $R:\mathcal A\simeq\prod_b\mathcal A_b$ with the actual restriction functors as coordinates. It is additive and preserves kernels and cokernels, whose universal properties transfer through a fully faithful, essentially surjective functor. So $R$ detects subobjects, quotients and isomorphisms.

source.place: Penultimate paragraph: extend the component filtrations by zero and concatenate them, even when their weights differ.

proof.text: For a component $b$, let $e_bL$ denote the tuple with $L$ in coordinate $b$ and zero elsewhere. Under the underlying restriction equivalence, $h_{b!}$ is insertion $e_b$. Indeed the open adjunction $h_{b!}\dashv h_b^*$ of [lem-zl-open-weil-unit-and-empty-fibre] identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(h_{b!}L,M)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(L,h_b^*M)$, while in product coordinates $\operatorname{Hom}(e_bL,rM)$ is that same Hom set, all other factors being singletons. The arrows corresponding to the identity maps under these natural bijections compose to identities, so they identify the two objects naturally. Its $b$-coordinate is the specified open unit $L\xrightarrow{\sim}h_b^*h_{b!}L$, which the same node states is a Weil isomorphism. The other coordinates are zero and have unique structure maps. Consequently $R(h_{b!}L)\simeq e_bL$ as Weil objects. By [lem-zl-immersion-weil-local-behavior](2), these are objects of the constructible hearts, and $h_{b!}$ is exact.

source.place: Penultimate paragraph: extend the component filtrations by zero and concatenate them, even when their weights differ.

proof.text: Put $H_b=h_b^*H$ and $M_b=\sum_{c<b}n_c$. For $0\le s\le n_b$, take the subobject of $R(H)=(H_c)_c$ whose coordinate is $H_c$ for $c<b$, $G_{b,s}$ for $c=b$, and zero for $c>b$, with the identity, prescribed inclusion, and zero maps into $H_c$, respectively. Lift this subobject through $R$ to a subobject $F_{M_b+s}\subseteq H$. Full faithfulness lifts its inclusions uniquely, and equality of maps is checked coordinatewise. The end of one block is the beginning of the next because $G_{b,n_b}=H_b$ and $G_{b+1,0}=0$. Hence these are one increasing filtration, starting at $0$ and ending at $H$, with exactly $\sum_b n_b$ arrows. A block with $n_b=0$ has $H_b=0$ and contributes no arrows.

source.place: Penultimate paragraph: extend the component filtrations by zero and concatenate them, even when their weights differ.

proof.text: For $1\le s\le n_b$, the inclusion $F_{M_b+s-1}\to F_{M_b+s}$ has identity coordinates before $b$, the given $G_{b,s-1}\to G_{b,s}$ in coordinate $b$, and $0\to0$ afterwards. Its cokernel in product coordinates is therefore $e_bQ_{b,s}$: maps killing the inclusion vanish in each identity coordinate, and in coordinate $b$ factor uniquely through the given cokernel $Q_{b,s}$. Since $R$ preserves cokernels, step 2 identifies the actual Weil quotient with $h_{b!}Q_{b,s}$. Thus the factors have precisely the order first $b$, then $s$; no reordering or replacement of the prescribed component subobjects has occurred.

source.place: Penultimate paragraph: extend the component filtrations by zero and concatenate them, even when their weights differ.

proof.text: By [lem-zl-immersion-weil-local-behavior](2), at every closed point of $S_0$ lying in $V_{b,0}$ the stalk and local Frobenius of $h_{b!}Q_{b,s}$ are those of $Q_{b,s}$ with the same residue-field size; all other stalks vanish. By [def-weil-punctual-weights], the former eigenvalues have modulus $q_x^{v_{b,s}/2}$ and the zero stalk has no eigenvalues. Thus this zero extension is pure of the assigned weight $v_{b,s}$. A Weil isomorphism intertwines the local operators, carrying each nonzero eigenvector to a nonzero eigenvector with the same eigenvalue, so the quotient in step 4 is pure of that weight too. Every upper bound on the given labels is therefore retained, regardless of their relative order.

source.place: Penultimate paragraph: extend the component filtrations by zero and concatenate them, even when their weights differ.

proof.text: The construction permits repeated terms and zero quotients: the quotient of an identity inclusion is zero, whose purity condition is vacuous by [def-weil-punctual-weights]. An empty piece contributes only zero objects, by [lem-zl-weil-heart-localization-exact]. If $N=0$, the covering assumption gives $S_0=\varnothing$, and that node gives $H=0$; take its length-zero filtration. These also cover a zero sheaf with prescribed positive lengths: retain all the indicated repeated zero terms.

lean.statement: theorem clopen_prescribed_weil_filtration (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p) (Ω : Type v) [Field Ω] [Algebra (Padic l) Ω] [IsAlgClosure (Padic l) Ω] (iota : Ω ≃+* ℂ) (S₀ : Over (Spec (.of D.k₀))) [LocallyOfFiniteType S₀.hom] [QuasiCompact S₀.hom] [IsSeparated S₀.hom] (N : ℕ) (V₀ : Fin N → Over (Spec (.of D.k₀))) [∀ b, LocallyOfFiniteType (V₀ b).hom] [∀ b, QuasiCompact (V₀ b).hom] [∀ b, IsSeparated (V₀ b).hom] (h₀ : ∀ b, V₀ b ⟶ S₀) [∀ b, IsOpenImmersion (h₀ b).left] [∀ b, IsClosedImmersion (h₀ b).left] (cover : ⋃ b, Set.range (h₀ b).left = Set.univ) (disjoint : ∀ b c, b ≠ c → Disjoint (Set.range (h₀ b).left) (Set.range (h₀ c).left)) (H : sfCommonStageWeilSheaf D l hl S₀ Ω) (n : Fin N → ℕ) (G : ∀ b, Fin (n b + 1) → sfCommonStageWeilSheaf D l hl (V₀ b) Ω) (φ : ∀ (b : Fin N) (s : Fin (n b)), G b s.castSucc ⟶ G b s.succ) (weights : ∀ b, Fin (n b) → ℝ) (start : ∀ b, IsZero (G b 0)) (finish : ∀ b, Nonempty (G b (Fin.last (n b)) ≅ (zlWeilPull D l hl Ω (h₀ b)).obj H)) (inclusions : ∀ b s, Mono (φ b s)) (pure : ∀ b s, SfIsPunctuallyPureOfWeight D l hl Ω (V₀ b) iota (cokernel (φ b s)) (weights b s)) : ∃ (J : ∀ b : Fin N, sfCommonStageWeilSheaf D l hl (V₀ b) Ω ⥤ sfCommonStageWeilSheaf D l hl S₀ Ω) (_adj : ∀ b, J b ⊣ zlWeilPull D l hl Ω (h₀ b)), ∃ (F : Fin ((∑ b, n b) + 1) → sfCommonStageWeilSheaf D l hl S₀ Ω) (ψ : ∀ t : Fin (∑ b, n b), F t.castSucc ⟶ F t.succ) (position : ∀ b, Fin (n b) → Fin (∑ c, n c)), IsZero (F 0) ∧ Nonempty (F (Fin.last (∑ b, n b)) ≅ H) ∧ (∀ t, Mono (ψ t)) ∧ (∀ b s, (position b s).val = (∑ c : Fin N, if c < b then n c else 0) + s.val) ∧ (∀ b s, Nonempty (cokernel (ψ (position b s)) ≅ (J b).obj (cokernel (φ b s))) ∧ SfIsPunctuallyPureOfWeight D l hl Ω S₀ iota (cokernel (ψ (position b s))) (weights b s)) ∧ (∀ w : ℝ, (∀ b s, weights b s ≤ w) → SfIsMixedOfWeightsAtMost D l hl Ω S₀ iota H w) ∧ (N = 0 → IsEmpty S₀.left ∧ IsZero H)
